facts.text: On this date in 1978, the Camp David Accords were signed — the first peace treaty between Israel and any Arab nation, brokered by a US president who had never visited the Middle East before taking office.
On this date in 1787, the US Constitution was signed by 39 delegates. Three present refused to sign, including George Mason, who objected that it lacked a bill of rights.
Monaco has a higher density of millionaires than any country on Earth — roughly one in three residents qualifies — yet it maintains a fully staffed army of 82 soldiers.
The world's largest city by land area is not Tokyo or Beijing. It is Hulunbuir, a prefecture-level city in Inner Mongolia, covering 263,000 sq km — larger than the United Kingdom.
More people live inside a 40km radius of Manila than in the entire country of Australia, making Metro Manila one of the most densely populated urban regions ever measured.
On this date in 1792, the Buttonwood Agreement was signed under a tree on Wall Street, creating what would become the New York Stock Exchange. Twenty-four brokers, one tree, no regulators.
On September 17, 2008, the U.S. Treasury announced it would guarantee money market funds after the Reserve Primary Fund 'broke the buck' — a run so severe it nearly froze global commerce in 72 hours.

The Dutch East India Company, often called history's most valuable corporation, issued the world's first tradeable shares in 1602. At peak valuation, it was worth roughly $8 trillion in today's dollars.

Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway originally made textiles. He later called buying it the worst trade of his life — a $200M mistake that cost him, by his own estimate, $200 billion in compounded opportunity.
The entire U.S. stock market lost more value on Black Monday, October 1987, in a single day than during the entire 1929 crash. The Dow fell 22.6% before lunch.
On this date in 1683, Antonie van Leeuwenhoek reported single-celled life to the Royal Society — the first human to see another organism's entire world fit on a pinhead.
Your skeleton is not static. Every 10 years, your bones have completely replaced themselves, atom by atom, through a process called remodeling.
On September 17, 1789, the U.S. Constitution was ratified — but the ink used to sign it contained iron gall, a compound still decaying and slowly eating the parchment today.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
The human eye can detect a single photon of light in total darkness. Your visual system is operating at the absolute physical limit of sensitivity.
On this day in 1787, the U.S. Constitution was signed — a document older than the Eiffel Tower, the bicycle, and the electric light bulb.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid.
On this day in 1862, Antietam became the bloodiest single day in American history — more Union soldiers died than in the entire War of 1812.
The fax machine was patented in 1843, before anyone had laid a single mile of transcontinental railroad track in North America.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded.

Saudade (Portuguese): a melancholic longing for something beloved and lost. Untranslatable into most languages, it became the emotional core of fado music and an unofficial Portuguese national feeling.
Hiraeth (Welsh): homesickness for a home you cannot return to — or one that never existed. The word collapses nostalgia, grief, and yearning into a single syllable cluster English has never managed.
On this date in 1787, the U.S. Constitution was signed. The word 'democracy' appears nowhere in it — the framers preferred 'republic,' a distinction they considered anything but semantic.
Meraki (Greek): the act of pouring your soul into something you make. Derived from the Turkish 'merak,' meaning love or longing, it describes the invisible residue a maker leaves in their work.

Mamihlapinatapai (Yaghan): a look shared between two people who both want something but neither will initiate. Linguists consider it one of the most precise words ever coined for a universal human moment.
On this date in 2017, China's central bank ordered all domestic cryptocurrency exchanges to shut down by September 30 — Bitcoin dropped 30% in two weeks, then tripled within three months.
On this date in 2022, Ethereum completed The Merge, switching from proof-of-work to proof-of-stake and cutting the network's energy consumption by approximately 99.95%.
Bitcoin's timelock opcode, OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY, sat unused in the codebase for years before being activated in BIP 65 — Satoshi had included it in the original 2009 release.
The $55M DAO hack of 2016 didn't technically break Ethereum's rules — the attacker used a legitimate reentrancy pattern. The hard fork to reverse it was a social override, not a protocol fix.
Miner Extractable Value (MEV) has extracted over $1.3 billion from Ethereum users since 2020 through sandwich attacks and front-running — all fully visible on-chain, none of it illegal.

On this date in 2009, Fei-Fei Li's team began the ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge—the competition that, three years later, AlexNet would win by a margin so large it effectively ended classical computer vision research.
Today in 2016, Google announced that its neural machine translation system had reduced translation errors by 60% overnight, a single deployment erasing years of incremental BLEU score gains.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 GWh of electricity—comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 average US households, all spent before a single query was served.

The term 'artificial intelligence' was coined for a 1956 Dartmouth workshop proposal written by John McCarthy, who chose it specifically to distance the field from Norbert Wiener's rival framing of 'cybernetics.'

Transformers were not invented for language: the 2017 'Attention Is All You Need' paper targeted machine translation, and its authors expected the architecture to remain a specialized NLP tool rather than the substrate of modern AI.
